messages:
maria: Quick idea — a tiny 'pin-manifest' helper + a deploy-bot flag to enforce a change-window safety window. aim: reduce copy/paste in release notes + make pin/rollback atomic.

maria: proposal sketch: a 1-file manifest that lists service pins, rollout policy, and an optional safety window. then a single deploy-bot command consumes it.

dan: example command?

maria: `deploy-bot pin --manifest=release-pin.yaml --apply` or `deploy-bot pin --manifest=release-pin.yaml --dry-run`

ashley: love the dry-run. can we also get a `--hold-until` that ties into calendar windows?

maria: yep. thinking `--safety-window=PT30M` (ISO 8601 duration) to mean do not auto-roll unpinned changes for 30m after rollout start. also `--hold-until=2026-04-01T15:00Z` to lock until change window opens.

kai: show a minimal manifest sample?

maria: ```yaml
# release-pin.yaml
services:
  - name: api-gateway
    version: v2.4.1
    rollout: canary
    canary_pct: 5
  - name: embeddings-worker
    version: v1.12.0-quant
rollout_policy:
  max_unhealthy: 1
  rollback_on_errors: true
safety:
  safety_window: PT20M
  hold_until: 2026-04-01T15:00:00Z
notes: |
  quick pin for customer X; watch latency spikes in first 15m
```

maria: The deploy-bot behavior: read manifest, apply pins, create release note stub, start rollout with canary percentage and safety_window enforced.

dan: What about rollback ergonomics? single `deploy-bot rollback --manifest=release-pin.yaml`?

maria: yes. we'll add `manifest.rollback_version` optional field and `--force` override. default behavior is graceful rollback to previous stable version recorded in service metadata.

ashley: We should auto-generate a small release note and attach to the release thread. Sample: "Pinned api-gateway->v2.4.1, embeddings-worker->v1.12.0-quant; canary 5%; safety-window 20m."

maria: exactly — deploy-bot will post the stub in the channel and create a permalink to the pinned manifest in S3.

kai: concern: permissions. Only owners of change should be allowed to `--apply`. Suggest adding `allowed_approvers` to manifest and have deploy-bot check against an ACL.

maria: good call. add `approvers: ["@maria","@dan"]` to manifest and deploy-bot validates via org directory.

dan: Implementation sketch: small Go CLI that validates manifest, signs it (short HMAC), uploads to releases bucket, then invokes bot webhook with `manifest_url` + `signature` + `dry_run` flag. Bot performs safety checks and posts summary.

maria: here's a rough deploy-bot CLI flow:
```
# validation
pin-manifest validate release-pin.yaml
# upload + sign
pin-manifest publish release-pin.yaml --out s3://redwood-release-manifests/2026-04-01/release-pin.yaml
# trigger
deploy-bot pin --manifest-url=https://s3.../release-pin.yaml --signature=abc123 --apply
```

ashley: Nice. For quick rollbacks, can the bot keep a small per-service history so we can `deploy-bot revert api-gateway --to=v2.3.9`?

maria: yep store last N pins in metadata. default N=10. UI in console can show history and let you trigger revert which calls same bot flow.

dan: small UX nit: print human-friendly summary like `Pinned 2 services · canary 5% · safety 20m · approvers: 2` when done.

maria: +1. also add `--annotate "reason"` to command to capture short release note text.

deploy-bot: @maria proposal accepted for PoC. I'll add `--safety-window`, `--hold-until`, and manifest URL support to the next release candidate. :white_check_mark:

kai: i'll start a tiny PR for `pin-manifest` CLI repo. will include schema + validator + upload helper.

maria: thanks — can we try a playground run on staging next Tue during the maintenance window? ping me when PR is up. :rocket:
